item.title: Making bush kinder learning visible without turning it into a checklist
item.description: A child balancing across a log, negotiating a route with a friend or returning to a place after rain may be showing learning that is easy to miss in a conventional assessment record. Bush kinder educators face a familiar challenge: how to document that learning for children and families while preserving the open-ended character of outdoor play.

item.title: Why evidence-based ECEC practice needs more than a training session
item.description: Finding a promising approach is only the beginning of changing practice in an early childhood service. Staff need time to understand it, decide how it fits their setting, use it with children and revisit what is working. New findings from the Australian Education Research Organisation (AERO) put that process, rather than a one-off professional learning session, at the centre of improvement.

item.description: The new guide brings together advice on mealtimes, food education, family engagement and service leadership. Its six modules offer educators and providers a way to review what children experience around food each day.
